INDEPENDENT FULL READ — AMEND exact stable off-tree SHA-256 7f675eab082443777289095ddd37c0ec3556ed968e43018d6cdf628d09f100bd, 1016 lines, 8102 words, 60793 bytes. Digest matched before and after the end-to-end read. The prior illustrative-type and partial-draft C17 defects are repaired. Two concrete contract failures remain.

1. I independently confirm StoryAtlas source-stage finding against current core. Strict UTF-8 whitespace bytes decode to a real raw String and can carry a decoded identity/receipt; StorySource.fromText then rejects rawText.trim.isEmpty at core atlas.scala:118. The statement that V1 has no fallible boundary after decode is false, and SourceOutcome.Refused(original, failure) erases completed evidence. Required repair: the refused source branch can retain optional decoded identity plus receipt, with constructor laws decoded implies admitted original, canonical remains absent, and constructed requires all three. C2 needs before-intake, strict-decode failure, whitespace post-decode refusal, and constructed controls plus cross-root mutations. Exact public names remain open.

2. Transactional publication is not actually no-clobber under a race. The spec prechecks target absence and later says one atomic rename to the still-absent target, while also claiming an existing target is never overwritten. On this target platform the installed rename(2) contract says: if the destination exists, it is first removed; the exclusive variant RENAME_EXCL is the operation that returns EEXIST. A sequential existing-empty-directory court does not kill a check-then-rename implementation: another process can create an empty target after the final absence check and ordinary rename can replace it atomically. Atomic does not mean no-replace.

Narrow repair: require one parent-anchored atomic no-replace commit operation, not an absence check plus ordinary rename. If the platform cannot guarantee both atomicity and exclusion, return UnsupportedAtomicPublication. Add a barrier-controlled C18 mutant/court that creates an empty target after prevalidation and immediately before commit; publication must refuse, the competing target must survive byte-for-byte, no partial target may appear, and the prepared bundle/staging evidence remains unchanged. Apply the same anchored-parent discipline so a pathname-parent swap cannot redirect commit.

Everything else in this digest passes my blocker-class review: closed result/report/universe distinctions, exact StoryModelCodec reuse, three identities, partial delivery, manifest re-read before commit, ViewBasis refusal for mixed roots, complete HTML textual twin, projection separation, and report/semantic/delivery non-conflation. After these two repairs, ACCEPT. No dependency, public vocabulary, code, candidate, or landing authority follows.
